scope: single controlled development round trip; no PlayWorld score or SOTA claim
caveat: Commanded camera closure does not prove realized closure. Endpoint image similarity cannot establish world memory if the realized route fails.

visual_judge.prompt: Evaluate two anonymized world-model videos independently and then compare. Each was given the same image and fixed camera path. Commands by one-second chunk: ['WAIT', 'RIGHT', 'RIGHT', 'RIGHT', 'LEFT', 'LEFT', 'LEFT', 'WAIT']. RIGHT and LEFT yaw 60 degrees per second; W moves forward. Commands are NOT proof that motion happened. Inspect actual frames. Assess whether each video realizes a turnaround and return to the starting viewpoint; whether persistent landmark identity, any sign text, geometry and spatial layout match on return; and whether there are sudden jumps, frozen motion or implausible transitions. Distinguish camera-control failures from forgetting. Do not reward a similar final building if reaching it required a reset. Do not invent unseen geometry. Return English JSON with keys A and B (each with realized_round_trip: yes|no|uncertain, starting_place_recovered: yes|no|uncertain, discontinuity: yes|no|uncertain, visual_evidence, failure_classification), preference: A|B|tie|neither, confidence: low|medium|high, and reasoning. This is a diagnostic comparison, not a benchmark score.

A.visual_evidence: Frames 0-9 hold the starting view: a stone tower mill with lattice sails, a small rust-colored wind-rose wheel on the right, birch trees on the left and a fence. During RIGHT (about frames 10-39) the scene pans left in a plausible way. A dark gable-roofed post mill comes into view, then a brown barn, then a stone tower with a balcony and an arched door. During LEFT (frames 40 onward) the motion reverses: the balcony tower slides right and the barn returns. The dark post mill does not reappear on the way back. Around frames 46-50 it is replaced by unfamiliar lattice sails over the barn. The original wind-rose mill reappears around frames 51-59, close to the start framing near frame 57-59, which is early. The view then keeps panning left. The original mill smears off to the right with morphing sails and ends up cropped in a tower at the left edge (frames 60-64). Frame 64 to 65 shows a scale and position jump. The video settles (frames 65-78) on a different mill: an evenly coursed stone drum, a brick-arched brown door at the base, no wind-rose wheel, different sails, open field to the left and no birch trees.
A.failure_classification: Mixed. The outbound yaw is well realized. On the return, the start view is passed well before the LEFT phase ends, so the return pan overshoots and/or the revisited content is compressed. The mill visible at the end is a hallucinated new landmark, not the start mill. The intermediate post mill was also forgotten and replaced. Some transition artifacts appear: sail morphing and a scale jump around frames 64-65.

B.visual_evidence: Frames 0-~43 are essentially identical to A: the same start view and the same rightward pan past the dark post mill, barn and balcony tower. On the LEFT return, B does bring back a dark gabled wooden mill structure with a long beam near the barn (frames 44-52). It is geometrically distorted (tilted, warped roof) but plausibly the same post mill landmark. The original wind-rose tower mill with birch trees then returns (frames 52-60), with framing near frames 57-59 similar to the start. The pan continues left past it: new wooden sheds and outbuildings appear that were never seen at the start (frames 60-64). The video settles (frames 65-78) on a different conical-roof mill with a green door, sheds on both sides, bare sail poles and no wind-rose wheel. The transitions are smoother than in A, with no obvious single-frame jump, but there is heavy geometric warping of the post mill.
B.failure_classification: Mixed. The outbound yaw is well realized. The return pan reaches the start view early and then overshoots or keeps rotating. At the end it lands on a hallucinated landmark with new surrounding buildings, which is a forgetting/hallucination failure at the endpoint. Memory of the intermediate landmark (the post mill) is partially retained, though distorted.

result.reasoning: Both videos share an identical, plausible outbound right turn and both reverse direction on LEFT. Both briefly pass a view resembling the starting mill partway through the LEFT phase, then continue panning. Both end on a different mill: A's has a brick-arched brown door, B's a green door with sheds. Neither recovers the starting viewpoint or the wind-rose landmark at the end, so neither earns credit for the final frame. B is marginally better as a diagnostic: it re-presents the dark post mill on the return path, while A replaces it with unrelated sails. B's transitions are also somewhat smoother than A's morphing and scale jump around frames 64-65. The core failure, an end-state hallucination after overshooting, is shared, so the preference is weak.
